## Review
When I first heard about the show's concept, my immediate question was <mark>whether this was even legally feasible</mark>.  
Even though they framed it as filming a documentary, from the restaurants' perspective, it felt bordering on outright fraud, which genuinely made me a bit worried.  
Still, I figured someone at the executive level must have known about the actual premise beforehand and cooperated.  

I usually enjoy cooking shows quite a bit, so I initially put it on in the background while doing other things without expecting much, but it turned out to be far more immersive and enjoyable than I had anticipated.  
```adcard
```
What impressed me most was how warmly the locals welcomed and consistently treated this unfamiliar outsider who suddenly arrived in a new environment.  
Watching them tell white lies to keep his spirits up and <mark>patiently teach him step by step</mark> truly warmed my heart.  

Throughout the show, however, I couldn't shake the feeling that the ultimate mission set by the production was simply too absurd.  
Honestly, while filming, neither the crew nor the cast likely believed the mission could actually succeed.  
I was left wishing they had set a slightly more realistic or achievable challenge instead.  
```adcard
```
Even so, thanks to <mark>the remarkable kindness and warmth of the coworkers</mark> working alongside him, the show constantly brought a smile to my face and left me feeling uplifted.  

Now that a spin-off is coming where the colleagues who worked hard together visit Korea, I'm already quite excited to see how it turns out.
